name: FL-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: No polling or expert ratings; markets price ~95% Republican
First-quarter incumbent with outside spending support
model.rationale: The district's R+18 lean, Patronis's overwhelming financial edge, and prediction markets pricing the Republican near 95% all point to a safe hold; the baseline margin of -17.4 needs little adjustment. Valimont's modest fundraising and lack of outside opposition spending give no evidence of a competitive race.
model.watch: Any unexpected scandal or a late surge of Democratic outside spending could narrow the margin, though a Republican loss remains highly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Florida's 1st District is one of the most Republican seats in the country, with a partisan lean of R+18. Incumbent Jimmy Patronis, who won the seat in a 2025 special election, is running for a full term and holds a commanding financial advantage, having raised roughly $3.8 million to Democrat Gay Valimont's $174,000. Outside groups have also spent over $2 million supporting Patronis, with no opposition spending against him.

Valimont has modest resources and no polling has been conducted in the race, so the forecast rests on the district's fundamentals. Prediction markets give Patronis about a 95% chance of winning. The expected margin is roughly 17 points Republican, consistent with the seat's lean, and the race is rated Safe Republican.
